rationale: Hebrews 7:1-2 (BSB) retells this exact scene in order, naming its people and acts: 'This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him, and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything' -- set beside Genesis 14:20's 'Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.' Hebrews 7:4-10 then builds an argument on the tithe ('Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder') and on the blessing ('the lesser is blessed by the greater'), and 7:3 builds on what Genesis does not record ('Without father or mother or genealogy'). Ellicott's commentary on Hebrews 7:1 notes that 'Of the facts recorded in Genesis none are passed over, except the gift of bread and wine,' a checkable omission both sides of the bread-and-wine dispute cite. Graded explicit_reference because Hebrews names the person, the place and the events with no citation formula, and explicit because no other passage in Scripture narrates a meeting of Abraham and Melchizedek; the type is kept at reference rather than type_antitype because Hebrews' own word is likeness ('like the Son of God,' 7:3), and how far that likeness reaches is the question the lesson's Positions section reports rather than settles.
